opportunities.title: Henry Moore Grants

amount.raw: Category maximums: New Projects and Commissions £20,000; Acquisitions and Collections £20,000; Conferences, Lectures and Publications £5,000; Long-Term Research grants £20,000; Research and Travel grants £2,500

opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK and international non-profit organisations (for New Projects and Commissions, Acquisitions and Collections, Conferences/Lectures/Publications, and Long-Term Research categories); individual sculpture historians, academics and conservators (Research and Travel category). Organisations must have operated as non-profits for at least 12 months. Individuals cannot apply to develop their own artistic practice.
opportunities.summary: Grants supporting the growth and development of sculpture across historical, modern and contemporary registers, and research that expands appreciation of sculpture. Categories cover exhibitions, commissions, acquisitions, conservation, conferences, publications and long-term research, plus research and travel grants for individual scholars.

opportunities.title: Visiting Research Fellowships

amount.raw: Accommodation plus travel/subsistence allocation: UK up to £600, Europe up to £700, Rest of world up to £1,000

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Academics or curators working on historic and contemporary sculpture (Research Fellowships at the Institute); researchers with interests in Henry Moore (fellowships at Studios & Gardens); artists (Artist Research Fellowships); established scholars (Senior Fellowships, six weeks).
opportunities.summary: Month-long research fellowships enabling artists and researchers to develop their work using the Henry Moore Institute in Leeds (Research Library, Archive of Sculptors' Papers, Leeds Sculpture Collections) or Henry Moore Studios & Gardens in Hertfordshire. No studio facilities offered. Applications closed for 2026/27; next round opens spring 2027.

opportunities.title: Dissertation Prize

amount.raw: BA dissertation £250 cash prize; MA dissertation £250 cash prize; plus £50 of selected publications and library deposit of copies

opportunities.eligibility_summary: BA and MA students of all disciplines who submitted a dissertation at a UK university within the past academic year. Dissertation must relate directly to sculpture and not have been previously published. Open to UK and international students as long as the dissertation was submitted to a UK university.
opportunities.summary: Two annual prizes for outstanding extended writing on contemporary, modern or historical sculpture, open to BA and MA students. Submissions for the 2026 prize will open in autumn.
